title: Safety Gate Fabric: per-dependency/model/tenant soft-hold with staged redirect and safe-fallback policy
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a unified "safety gate" fabric that lets us express circuit-breaker policies at three orthogonal dimensions: per-external-dependency (e.g., embeddings-db, auth-proxy), per-served-model (model variant and quantization), and per-tenant. The fabric must support soft-hold (probabilistic shedding), hard-trip, progressive redirection to fallbacks, and a bounded rollback window to avoid thrashing.

Scope:
- Runtime hook points to evaluate current health signals and SLO-derived error budgets for a request.
- Policy DSL for expressing trip thresholds (error rate, latency p95/p99, missing KV cache hit rate) and resulting actions (reject, probabilistic-shed=X%, route-to-fallback-model, downgrade-quantization).
- Staged fallback pipeline: 1) local-model degrade (lower precision), 2) sibling-model redirect, 3) region failover, 4) best-effort hosted proxy.
- Telemetry: per-policy time-series + alerting, and a new dashboard for policy churn + rollback reasons.

Design decisions and tradeoffs considered:
1) Centralized policy service vs distributed in-runtime evaluation: we are going with a hybrid: policies are authored and stored centrally but evaluated in the serving runtime with local cached copies to avoid control-plane latency. This reduces 2-hop decision latency at the expense of stronger versioning/consistency mechanics.
2) Deterministic thresholds vs probabilistic shedding: we'll support both. Deterministic trips for severe infra failures; probabilistic soft-hold for congestion to preserve best-effort for high-priority tenants.
3) Fallback cost accounting: fallbacks (e.g., switching to sibling higher-cost model) must be attributed to the originating tenant for billing and throttling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ability to define and deploy policies via Console and API; policies must propagate to runtime nodes within 30s.
- When a dependent DB crosses configured error-rate threshold, affected requests should be routed according to policy with <50ms additional median latency.
- End-to-end test harness that simulates dependency failures and verifies staged fallback sequence reliably in CI.
- Dashboard shows per-policy trip events and the top 3 root causes for automatic rollbacks.

Implementation plan: (milestones)
- Week 1: Policy DSL + storage; runtime API hooks scaffolding (ENG-76123.1).
- Week 2: Implement evaluation engine + local caching + unit tests (ENG-76123.2).
- Week 3: Integrate staged fallback routing and billing attribution (ENG-76123.3).
- Week 4: Canary rollouts to non-prod clusters, load testing, and observability polish (ENG-76123.4).

Testing strategy:
- Synthetic failure injection in chaos env: latency spikes, 5xx flood, KV cache evictions.
- Property-based tests for probabilistic-shed that ensure statistical guarantees (within 95% CI).
- End-to-end scenario tests that assert fallbacks are executed in the correct order and rollback hysteresis prevents flapping.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: policy staleness on nodes causing unexpected behavior. Mitigation: add versioned policy TTLs and automatic fetch-after-write with a conservative default policy on expiry.
- Risk: excessive fallback increases cost. Mitigation: billing attribution + per-tenant budget guardrails that can disable non-critical fallbacks when budgets exceeded.
- Risk: cascading failover across regions. Mitigation: rolling region-level trip locks and global rate-limits to control fanout.

- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CPB-2797-Safety+Gate+Fabric
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892
- Load test results (internal): https://dashboards.datadog.com/d/abc123/CB-Fabric-loadtests
- Incident that motivated work: Incident-2026-01-17 (auth-proxy partial outage) postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/notes/incident-2026-01-17-postmortem.pdf

Open questions:
- Should tenant-priority be a continuous score or discrete tiers? (Recommendation: discrete tiers initially.)
- How aggressively to attribute fallback cost to tenant vs platform for early-stage customers?

Next steps:

- Design: review the policy authoring UX and failure explanation text shown to users during canary (owner: Evan Brooks).
